title: Pentagon spokesperson says Pete Hegseth’s wife is ‘in full compliance with all ethics laws,’ calls concerns about her work with a consulting firm with alleged links to a military supplier ‘ridiculous slander’
content:
The Pentagon has defended Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and his wife, Jennifer Hegseth, after questions emerged over her consulting work for a Washington firm that has had defense contractor Lockheed Martin as a client.

Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said that both Hegseths are “in full compliance with all ethics laws and regulations” and dismissed suggestions of a conflict of interest as “ridiculous slander.”

There is no evidence that Jennifer worked directly with Lockheed Martin, advised the company on defense matters or influenced Pentagon decisions.

Pentagon says Hegseths followed ethics rules

The Pentagon defended Pete and Jennifer Hegseth following ethics questions regarding her consulting firm’s defense ties. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM/MEGA

Parnell said that “any insinuations or claims otherwise are ridiculous slander.”

He said the Department of Defense maintains a “rigorous, multilayered ethics framework” that includes financial disclosure reviews, divestitures when necessary and screening procedures designed to prevent conflicts of interest.

The Pentagon spokesperson said that “robust administrative firewalls” are also established and enforced when required. According to Parnell, those measures ensure senior officials are “completely screened from matters involving former employers or private interests.”

A spokesperson for Watchtower Strategy, the firm where she is listed as a consultant, told Newsweek that she “has not interfaced with any clients nor does she provide any advice to Watchtower on defense matters.”

Why Jennifer’s work raised questions

Pete Hegseth’s financial disclosure lists his wife as a consultant to Watchtower Strategy, a D.C. firm co-founded by Kevin McCarthy. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM/MEGA

Pete’s annual financial disclosure lists his wife as a consultant to Watchtower Strategy, a Washington public relations and advocacy firm.

The company was co-founded in early 2025 by former House Speaker Kevin McCarthy. Politico reported on November 4 that Watchtower was founded in January 2025 and that Lockheed Martin was among its clients that year.

The disclosure does not specify how much Jennifer was paid or whether she continues to work with the firm.

A Watchtower spokesperson said she assisted the company with “navigating conservative TV media.”

The spokesperson did not say whether that work is ongoing.

The available information does not establish that Jennifer had any direct relationship with Lockheed Martin or performed work for the defense contractor.

Hegseth faces political pressure

The questions about the consulting work emerged as Pete faced growing political pressure over the war with Iran and Republican losses in the November 3 midterm elections.

President Donald Trump said on November 5 that he had “every intention” of keeping Hegseth as defense secretary.

Hegseth also pushed back against the criticism in a video message that day, saying he would “not back down.”

Jennifer, a longtime former Fox News producer, has remained a visible presence alongside her husband.

In August, she was named chair of Trump’s Military Spouse Commission, a voluntary advisory position.

Her late father reportedly worked as an executive at Lockheed Martin, adding another point of interest to questions surrounding her professional and family connections to the defense industry.

However, the Pentagon and Watchtower have denied any suggestion that her consulting role created an ethics violation or gave her influence over Defense Department decisions.

title: Wisconsin infant dies after contracting measles, becomes first person in the state to die of the disease in nearly four decades
content:
An infant in southwestern Wisconsin has died after contracting measles, marking the state’s first death from the disease in 36 years, state health officials announced Thursday.

The death is the first measles-related death reported in Wisconsin since 1990 and comes as the state faces its largest measles outbreak in more than three decades.

What Wisconsin officials said

The Wisconsin Department of Health Services confirmed that the coroner determined measles as the immediate cause of death. By: CDC/UNSPLASH

The Wisconsin Department of Health Services said the coroner determined that measles was the immediate cause of death.

DHS Secretary Kirsten Johnson addressed the death in a statement.

“It is with a heavy heart we are reporting the first death of an infant connected with a measles outbreak in Wisconsin in many years,” Johnson said. “My heart is broken for the family.”

Johnson added that the death of any child is a tragedy, particularly when it involves a vaccine-preventable disease.

DHS did not disclose where the infant died or provide additional details, citing the family’s privacy.

Measles outbreak continues to grow

DHS confirmed the infant death was directly associated with an ongoing and expanding measles outbreak in southern Wisconsin. By: CDC/UNSPLASH

DHS said the death was associated with an ongoing measles outbreak in southern Wisconsin.

The state has reported 431 measles cases across 13 counties in 2026, the highest total in more than 35 years. Nine people have been hospitalized.

The outbreak has expanded steadily in recent months.

The outbreak in Grant, Iowa and Lafayette counties had produced 151 confirmed and six probable cases. DHS had confirmed 267 measles cases statewide, with the outbreak reaching Vernon County.

Wisconsin health officials had declared an outbreak in Lafayette and Iowa counties shortly before the fall school year began.

Dr. Ryan Westergaard, Wisconsin’s chief medical officer, told CNN that measles continues to spread because enough people remain susceptible to allow the virus to find new hosts.

Health officials say about 95 percent of the population needs to be vaccinated to maintain protection against measles. Two doses of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine are about 97 percent effective.

Other measles deaths reported nationwide

The Wisconsin death came days after two other measles-associated deaths were reported in the United States.

A child in New York’s Lewis County died Sunday, November 1, in the state’s first known measles-associated death in more than 30 years. State and local officials said the child was unvaccinated and died at the family’s home.

Pennsylvania reported another measles-associated death.

The person was an unvaccinated resident of Jefferson County. Funeral director Brenda Shumaker identified the person as a 21-year-old woman who suffered complications after giving birth at home.

CDC death count differs from state reports

There is a discrepancy between the number of measles deaths reported by states and the count published by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

The Washington Post reported that the CDC updated its website on November 4 to list four measles deaths in 2026.

Pennsylvania has reported six measles-associated deaths, while New York has reported one and Wisconsin has now reported one.

The CDC said it is working with state epidemiologists to establish a standardized definition for reporting measles deaths. The agency counts deaths that are confirmed and reported directly to it.

U.S. measles cases reach highest level since 1991

The CDC reports 5,182 measles cases in the United States in 2026, the highest annual total since 1991.

Pennsylvania is experiencing the country’s largest outbreak. As of November 4, the state had recorded 1,467 cases across 45 counties.

The national outbreak has also raised questions about the United States’ measles elimination status.

The Pan American Health Organization is scheduled to meet from November 10 to 13 to determine whether the United States will retain its measles elimination status. The country has held that designation since 2000.

No decision had been announced at the time of writing.

The Wisconsin infant’s death underscores the continuing impact of the nationwide measles resurgence as health officials work to contain outbreaks and prevent further deaths.

title: Attorney General Todd Blanche floats DOJ investigation after President Donald Trump accused Democratic lawmakers of ‘extortion at the highest level’ for threatening Republicans with impeachment
content:
Attorney General Todd Blanche left open the possibility that Democratic lawmakers could face a Department of Justice investigation after President Donald Trump ordered the department to examine what he described as threats, extortion and “lawfare” against administration officials, Republican donors and supporters.

Blanche did not announce an investigation or identify a federal criminal statute that Democratic lawmakers were suspected of violating.

What Blanche said on CNN

Todd Blanche left open the possibility that Democratic lawmakers could face DOJ investigations following Donald Trump’s directive. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM / MEGA

Appearing on CNN’s State of the Union, Blanche argued that some recent Democratic rhetoric went beyond legitimate congressional oversight. He declined to identify specific criminal conduct when host Dana Bash pressed him.

“You have free speech in this country,” Blanche said. “You are allowed to be critical of President Trump, of me, of this administration. But when the threats become so vile and so dangerous…at some point you have to draw the line.”

Bash then asked whether the DOJ would investigate lawmakers and whether the conduct described constituted a crime.

“It depends on what’s said. So yes, it could be,” Blanche replied. “I’m not saying that necessarily every case is going to be prosecuted.”

Asked about Trump’s characterization of Democrats as “extortionists” who belong in prison, Blanche said the answer depended on what laws had allegedly been broken.

“Well, it depends on what the crime is and what they’ve done,” he said.

Blanche said Trump was responding to Democratic rhetoric after the midterm elections.

“That is not government. That is not leading. That is not oversight,” he said.

Trump orders DOJ to investigate

Donald Trump demanded a DOJ investigation into Democrats in a Truth Social post. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM/MEGA

Trump made the demand in a Truth Social post on November 7, 2026.

He accused Democrats of threatening Blanche and other officials with impeachment and “many other forms of punishment.” He also alleged that Democratic lawmakers were targeting Republican donors “with imprisonment and many other levels of punishment, just because they happen to be Republicans, or Republican supporters.”

“This is extortion at the highest level and they should be held accountable for this,” Trump wrote. “This is Weaponization and Lawfare at another level.”

He added: “The imprisonment should be against these EXTORTIONISTS…By copy of this statement, I am ordering the Department of Justice to look into this criminal act, immediately!”

Slotkin responds to Trump

Donald Trump’s Truth Social post focused in part on Michigan Democratic Sen. Elissa Slotkin’s comments about administrative hiring. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM/MEGA

Trump’s post focused in part on Senator Elissa Slotkin, a Michigan Democrat.

Slotkin had discussed the possibility of future legal scrutiny discouraging people from joining the Trump administration during an October 13 event at the University of Chicago.

“I want young people coming out of school to say, ‘Should I go work for the Trump administration? … Lord, that might be buying myself a ton of problems that I don’t want and so let me avoid participating in that,’” Slotkin said. “I want that deterrence message.”

Slotkin rejected Trump’s accusations in a statement posted on X and emailed to Newsweek on November 7.

She said accountability should be based on whether someone broke the law rather than their political affiliation.

“If you break the law or use taxpayer dollars to enrich yourself, you should be held accountable,” Slotkin said. “If you didn’t break the law, then it’s all good.”

Blanche warns over Democratic oversight

Blanche also pointed to comments from incoming House Oversight Committee Chairman Robert Garcia, a California Democrat.

Garcia has promised an “aggressive” series of investigations into the Trump administration and the president’s family. He also warned incoming White House chief of staff Stephen Miller to “lawyer up.”

Blanche acknowledged that Congress has a constitutional role to conduct oversight.

“I welcome oversight. Oversight is exactly something they should be doing,” he said.

But he warned that the Justice Department would intervene if congressional investigations became what he described as improper targeting of White House officials.

“If they try to come after Stephen Miller for these whatever it is that Garcia thinks he’s going to do, instead of actually just conducting oversight and leading, of course the Department of Justice will be there to defend him,” Blanche said.

Raskin raises impeachment possibility

Rep. Jamie Raskin of Maryland, a Democrat who could chair the House Judiciary Committee in the next Congress, said Blanche himself could face impeachment hearings.

Speaking to MS NOW, Raskin cited Blanche’s handling of the Jeffrey Epstein case and what he described as the DOJ’s pursuit of Trump’s political opponents.

“The Department of Justice has clearly become a Department of Injustice — an instrument of revenge, political revenge for the president,” Raskin said. “… This attorney general has been doing nothing other than acting in his old capacity as a personal criminal defense attorney to Donald Trump.”

Divided government sets up new clash

The exchange points to a growing confrontation between the Trump administration and congressional Democrats after the November 3 midterm elections.

Democrats won control of both the House and Senate, giving them subpoena power and the ability to launch investigations into the administration when the new Congress begins in January 2027.

The shift creates divided government for the final two years of Trump’s term and sets up potential clashes over congressional oversight, executive power and the Justice Department.

title: ‘Not going to happen’: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries refuses to work with Stephen Miller after President Donald Trump appointed him as White House chief of staff, says ‘it’s an awful choice’
content:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries ruled out working with Stephen Miller after President Donald Trump named the longtime immigration hard-liner his new White House chief of staff.

Speaking Sunday on ABC News’ This Week, the New York Democrat said Democrats could still look for areas of cooperation with Trump, but drew a firm line at Miller.

“It’s an awful choice,” Jeffries said. “Stephen Miller is the architect of Donald Trump’s violent mass deportation machine.”

Jeffries draws a line at Miller

Jeffries said Democrats could seek areas of agreement with Trump following their sweeping victories in the November 3 midterm elections.

But he said Miller’s appointment would make the type of communication he previously had with outgoing Chief of Staff Susie Wiles impossible.

“It was an irresponsible decision in my view,” Jeffries told host Jonathan Karl. “There’s not going to be an opportunity, certainly, to work with Stephen Miller and what he represents.”

Karl asked whether Jeffries would continue regular communication with Miller as he had with Wiles.

“It’s not going to happen with the new chief of staff,” Jeffries said.

He also grouped Miller with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and other administration officials whom he described as representing “a really toxic brand of political engagement, of politics and of governance.”

Jeffries attacks Miller’s immigration record

Jeffries accused Miller of helping direct administration policies that he said used “billions of taxpayer dollars to brutalize and kill American citizens, like Alex Pretti and Renee Nicole Good.”

He also accused the administration of policies that “violently target law-abiding, immigrant families and communities all across the country.”

Jeffries said Democrats remained “committed to forcefully pushing back against the extremism that they may try to continue to unleash on the American people.”

He argued that the midterm results created “a firewall in the House and a firewall in the Senate,” saying voters rejected “that kind of MAGA extremism.”

The election produced Republican losses across House, Senate, gubernatorial and state legislative races.

White House defends Miller

White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said in an emailed statement Sunday that Trump remained willing to work with Democrats.

“As the President has said, he’s willing to work with anyone to continue delivering victories for hardworking Americans,” Bis said. “If Democrats choose to not work with the Administration, they are choosing to work against the American people.”

Bis defended Miller’s record and role in the administration.

“Stephen Miller has been a key player in delivering on President Trump’s America First agenda since day one,” she said.

Bis credited Miller with spearheading the administration’s crime crackdown in Washington and Memphis, deregulation efforts, its energy agenda, efforts to dismantle drug cartels and border security policies.

“In his new role, he will continue to deliver historic successes for the American people,” she said.

Miller pledges loyalty to Trump

Miller spoke at Mar-a-Lago on Friday after Trump announced that he would replace Wiles with Miller, who previously served as deputy chief of staff for policy.

Miller called his appointment “the privilege of a lifetime to join President Trump.”

“If it wasn’t for President Trump, the United States of America would not exist right now,” he said.

“This man saved America,” Miller added. “He saved our military from collapse, he saved our economy from destruction, he saved our border from annihilation and he saved our country from threats at home and abroad which would have been the end of the American dream forever.”

Miller later pledged his loyalty to Trump.

“I pledge to you Mr. President my absolute loyalty, my unwavering commitment and my total devotion to your success and the success of this country,” he said.

A divided Washington

Trump announced Miller’s appointment Friday, November 6. Miller has been one of the principal architects of Trump’s immigration agenda, including the administration’s first-term travel ban and broader immigration and federal spending policies.

The appointment came after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections amid voter dissatisfaction with Trump’s economic and domestic policies.

Associated Press voter polling indicated notable shifts toward Democrats among Latino and younger voters. Jeffries could become the next speaker of the House when Democrats take control of the chamber in January.

Trump had warned before the election that he would become “Mr. Veto” if Democrats took control of Congress. Overriding a presidential veto requires two-thirds support in both the House and Senate.

Trump has also indicated that he is open to negotiating with Democrats. He said in a 60 Minutes interview scheduled to air Sunday that he would be willing to make deals with the opposition party.

Republicans will retain control of Congress during the lame-duck session before Democrats assume their majorities in January 2027.

The shift leaves Jeffries and Trump with potential areas for cooperation, but Jeffries has made clear that Miller will not be part of that equation.

title: ‘Pete Hegseth has got to go’: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries backs Republican-led effort to impeach the secretary of defense, says he ‘abused his power’ and ‘undermined our national security’
content:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, a New York Democrat, declared himself a “hard yes” on impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. He said the Pentagon chief “Pete Hegseth has got to go,” aligning House Democratic leadership with a Republican-led push to remove one of President Donald Trump’s closest national security allies.

What Jeffries said and where

Jeffries made the remarks during an interview. Co-anchor Jonathan Karl asked whether he was confident all House Democrats would join him in backing the resolution.

Jeffries said Hegseth had “abused his power” and “undermined our national security.” He also accused him of engineering “this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran,” which he said had driven up prices for Americans and left the country less safe.

Jeffries did not promise a unified caucus. He said House Democrats would discuss the matter on Tuesday, November 10, when they reconvene in Washington for the first time since the midterm elections. However, he predicted “incredibly strong support” for the resolution.

Massie’s resolution and the timeline

The effort is led by outgoing Rep. Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican. Massie told ABC News he intends to reintroduce a privileged resolution to impeach Hegseth as early as Monday, November 9. Fox News reported that Massie was expected to re-trigger the resolution on the afternoon of November 9, which would require a House vote within two legislative days, by Wednesday, November 11.

Massie’s 34-page resolution contains eight articles of impeachment. Article I alleges that Hegseth executed unlawful orders in violation of Section 2(c) of the War Powers Resolution of 1973. It argues that Congress holds the constitutional power to initiate war. It also alleges U.S. forces were put into hostilities without a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization or an attack on the United States. Later articles lay out further War Powers claims, along with allegations involving civilian casualties and extrajudicial killings.

Why the vote is returning

Massie first moved against Hegseth in September. He introduced his eight articles on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, using a privileged resolution so that Speaker Mike Johnson would have to act within 48 hours before the House left for recess.

Johnson then sent members home for a seven-week campaign recess, pushing any impeachment vote past the midterm elections. Johnson told reporters the early departure had nothing to do with Hegseth and said the House would take up Massie’s resolution after the elections, where it would “immediately be tabled.”

Because the two-day clock lapsed during the recess, Massie has to start the process over. He has said there is “one contingency” in which he would not reintroduce the articles: Hegseth resigns. Massie also said on social media that his resolution is “a much gentler version” of what is coming when Democrats control Congress and that Democrats would “have hearings & trials.”

The midterm backdrop

Voters went to the polls on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. NBC News reported that no minority party had flipped control of both chambers on a single night since 2006. Democrats flipped Senate seats in Kansas, Iowa, Texas, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina, according to Northeastern Global News. As of Sunday, November 8, the Associated Press showed Democrats with 54 Senate seats to 44 for Republicans and 254 House seats to 162 for Republicans, with 19 House races still uncalled.

Analysts largely attributed the Democratic wins to voter dissatisfaction over the U.S. war with Iran, rising gas prices and broader economic anxieties. Gas prices spiked after Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu launched the war in late February, according to NBC News. CBS News reported that gas prices on Election Day were the highest in the history of Election Day.

Vice President J.D. Vance, in a post on X the day after the election, put it bluntly: “The reason we lost is the war.” Asked about Vance’s view, Trump said it was “largely true” because the war had pushed gasoline prices up.

Republicans weigh in

Since the election, some Republicans have signaled openness to impeachment. House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer, a Kentucky Republican, “there’s a lot of questions about Hegseth.” Sen. Thom Tillis, a North Carolina Republican, told CBS News that Hegseth faces “a reckoning.”

Axios reported on November 8 that House Republican leaders were bracing for enough GOP defections to impeach Hegseth, noting that Republicans who lost re-election could be more willing to vote for it. Rep. Don Bacon, a Nebraska Republican, told Axios he was undecided. The Washington Times reported that GOP leaders were expected to move to kill the resolution, though it was not certain all Republicans would vote to do so.

Hegseth and the Pentagon respond

Hegseth addressed the effort in a video posted to X on Thursday, November 5. CNN reported it was filmed outside the Defense Department. He called Massie “a disgruntled, defeated congressman” and described the articles as a “sham” impeachment, comparing them to the two impeachments of Trump.

Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said in an email that Hegseth “will not back down or be deterred by politicians seeking to score partisan points.” He added that the Department of War has followed the law and that Hegseth is “100% committed” to leading the department until the end of Trump’s term.

Asked whether he was considering replacing Hegseth, Trump replied, “No, I think he’s doing a very good job.” The White House said Trump retained “full confidence” in the defense secretary.

What happens next

Once Massie moves to force the vote, Johnson can put the resolution on the floor, hold a vote to refer it to committee, or move to table it. Impeaching a Cabinet official requires a simple majority in the House. Conviction and removal require two-thirds of senators present, or 67 votes if all 100 vote. Because the new Congress is not sworn in until January, any vote in the lame-duck session would occur under the current Republican majority. If the resolution fails, incoming Democratic majorities could open investigations or renew impeachment proceedings after taking control.

title: Trump’s new White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller calls Republican Party ‘more popular than ever,’ says ‘the United States of America would not exist right now’ if not for the president
content:
Stephen Miller declared the Republican Party “more popular than ever” and credited President Donald Trump with saving the United States during his first public remarks as the new White House chief of staff.

Speaking November 6 at a Conservative Political Action Conference event at Mar-a-Lago in Florida, Miller said the country “would not exist right now” without Trump.

His remarks came just 72 hours after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the November 3 midterm elections, giving Miller’s defense of the president added significance as Republicans confront the scale of their losses.

Miller pledges loyalty to Trump

Stephen Miller declared the Republican Party “more popular than ever” just 72 hours after midterm election losses. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM / MEGA

Miller said it was “the privilege of a lifetime to join President Trump” after being selected to replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff.

“If it wasn’t for President Trump, the United States of America would not exist right now,” Miller said.

“This man saved America,” he added. “He saved our military from collapse, he saved our economy from destruction, he saved our border from annihilation and he saved our country from threats at home and abroad which would have been the end of the American dream forever.”

Miller also pointed to the July 2024 assassination attempt against Trump in Butler, Pennsylvania and the criminal prosecutions the president has faced.

“This man took a bullet for us, he faced down life in prison for us, he saved the Republican Party,” Miller said.

He added that Trump had made the party “stronger and more popular and more resilient than ever before.”

Miller ended his speech with a direct pledge to Trump.

“I pledge to you Mr. President my absolute loyalty, my unwavering commitment and my total devotion to your success and the success of this country,” he said.

Republicans face a major midterm setback

Donald Trump acknowledged that economic issues and the war in Iran contributed significantly to Republican election losses. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM/MEGA

Miller’s comments came after Republicans suffered significant losses in the midterm elections.

Republicans lost more than 40 House seats and at least seven Senate seats. The Associated Press reported that Democrats flipped seven Senate seats and held a 54-44 advantage, with two races still undecided.

Trump has acknowledged that the economy and the war in Iran contributed to the Republican losses.

He also argued that the result would have been different if he had been on the ballot.

“I JUST WASN’T ON THE BALLOT. IF I WERE, WE WOULD HAVE WON IN A LANDSLIDE!” Trump said.

Miller’s remarks offered a sharply different message from Republicans who have called for changes to the party’s approach after the defeat.

Miller’s growing influence in the White House

Stephen Miller’s deep understanding of executive authority signals a likely surge in unilateral executive actions by Trump. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM / MEGA

Miller, 41, joined Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign as a speechwriter and became one of the president’s most influential advisers.

He was a principal architect and public defender of Trump’s aggressive immigration policies and has played a major role in shaping the administration’s approach to executive power.

Miller’s deep understanding of presidential authority could lead to an increase in executive actions during the final two years of Trump’s second term.

White House Communications Director Steven Cheung previously described Miller as a longtime Trump ally.

“Stephen Miller is a Trump OG, someone who has been with the President since the very beginning. There is no bigger advocate for the Trump agenda than Stephen and he will help the Administration deliver on monumental victories for the rest of this historic second term,” Cheung said.

Miller’s promotion also signals that Trump is not necessarily preparing for a more conciliatory approach toward Democrats who are preparing to investigate his administration.

Miller himself is among the officials Democrats have targeted for scrutiny.

Trump praises Byron Donalds

Donald Trump publicly praised Byron Donalds at Kennedy Space Center after Donalds won the Florida gubernatorial election. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM/MEGA

Before the Mar-a-Lago event, Trump praised Republican Representative Byron Donalds during a visit to the Kennedy Space Center.

Donalds defeated Democrat David Jolly in Florida’s gubernatorial race and will succeed Ron DeSantis as governor.

“He won,” Trump said. “He won it and he did it the hard way, he worked. He worked hard.”

The praise came as DeSantis sharply criticized Republicans following the midterm losses.

DeSantis turns on the GOP

DeSantis criticized the party’s handling of the Iran war and its impact on voters during an appearance on Straight Shooter with Stephen A. Smith, released November 2.

He called the war a “big, big drag” on Republicans and accused party leaders of misleading voters about higher gas prices.

“That’s just the fact,” DeSantis said. “If you can’t admit that to voters, then you’re gaslighting them and they’re not going to listen to you on other things.”

At a news conference in Tallahassee on November 4, DeSantis described the election results as “close to an extinction-level event” for Republicans in many parts of the country.

His criticism has fueled speculation that he could make another bid for the White House after losing the 2024 Republican nomination to Trump.

DeSantis is term-limited and will leave the Florida governor’s office in January 2027.

Asked about a possible presidential campaign in an interview released November 2, he kept the possibility open.

“We’ll see what happens,” DeSantis said. “Maybe someday. I don’t know about ’28. Maybe later. Maybe. We’ll see.”

With Miller now positioned as Trump’s chief of staff and Republicans divided over how to respond to their midterm defeat, the competing messages highlight a broader debate over whether the party should double down on Trump’s approach or begin charting a different path.

title: Trump gets surprise boost as Department of Labor numbers show U.S. jobs market is stronger than believed prior to the midterms: The president’s ‘pro-growth economic agenda is working,’ White House says
content:
The U.S. jobs market showed more strength than expected before the November 3 midterm elections, giving President Donald Trump a fresh economic talking point just days after voters handed Democrats control of Congress.

U.S. nonfarm payroll employment increased by 165,000 in October, while September’s job gain was revised sharply higher from 29,000 to 60,000, according to Department of Labor data released Friday.

The figures far exceeded expectations. Economists surveyed for FactSet had forecast a gain of 65,000 jobs and an unemployment rate of 4.2 percent.

What the jobs report showed

The Bureau of Labor Statistics said the unemployment rate fell to 4.1 percent in October from 4.2 percent in September.

Job gains were concentrated in professional and business services, health care and transportation and warehousing.

The BLS also revised August’s job gain upward by 53,000 to 186,000 and September’s by 31,000 to 60,000. Combined, the revisions made the two previous months 84,000 jobs stronger than initially reported.

Health care added 42,000 jobs in October, compared with an average monthly gain of 31,000 over the previous 12 months.

Professional and business services added 70,000 jobs, far above its 12-month average of 15,000.

The economy has averaged 86,100 jobs a month so far in 2026, according to BLS data.

White House touts economic agenda

The White House quickly seized on the report as evidence that Trump’s economic policies were producing results.

The administration called the figures “proof that President Trump’s pro-growth economic agenda is working.”

“President Trump’s mission remains unchanged: lowering costs, creating jobs, boosting our economy and putting American workers first,” White House spokesman Matthew Middleton told Newsweek on Friday.

The strong employment figures provide the administration with a positive economic message after Republicans suffered major losses in the midterm elections.

Economists see encouraging signs

Economists broadly described the report as encouraging, although some warned that wages and inflation remain bigger concerns for households.

Angelo Kourkafas, senior global strategist at Edward Jones, called it a “blowout jobs report,” pointing to stronger payroll growth, upward revisions, the lower unemployment rate and improved labor-force participation.

Seema Shah, chief global strategist at Principal Asset Management, wrote that the data were “a strong rebuttal” to concerns about a meaningful economic slowdown.

Ger Doyle, regional president for North America at workforce solutions company ManpowerGroup, said employers were adding jobs faster than many had expected.

But Doyle cautioned that the next question is whether the strength spreads across more industries before it can be described as a broader hiring recovery.

Jared Bernstein, who chaired the Council of Economic Advisers under former President Joe Biden, said on Substack that the report did not appear to be an obvious one-off, although more data were needed.

He said the job market looked more solid than it had a few months earlier.

Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, also called the figures a “blowout jobs report” in a post on X.

She added that inflation had erased wage gains for seven consecutive months, highlighting the continued pressure facing households despite the strong employment figures.

Report comes after Democratic midterm victory

The jobs report arrived three days after Democrats won control of both the House and Senate.

The midterm campaign was shaped by voter concerns over the ongoing Iran war, inflation and the cost of living, with the results widely viewed as a rejection of Trump’s policies.

Democratic control of Congress will give the party greater power to challenge Trump’s legislative agenda and investigate his administration during the final two years of his second term.

Democrats are expected to take control of House committees in January 2027, giving them subpoena and oversight authority over the executive branch.

The strong jobs figures therefore arrive at a politically significant moment for Trump, offering the White House an economic counterpoint to the election results.

Markets look ahead to inflation data

The report followed a sharp market selloff Thursday, November 5, as investors worried that Democratic gains could slow the expansion of data centers.

The next major inflation report from the BLS is scheduled for Tuesday, November 10.

That data could provide another test of whether the stronger labor market is translating into broader economic stability for American households.

For now, the October employment report gives Trump and his administration a stronger economic narrative than many analysts expected heading into the midterms, even as Democrats prepare to use their new congressional majority to scrutinize his policies.

title: Journey Drummer Deen Castronovo Exits Band Mid-Tour Due to 'Health Matters'
content:
Journey is pushing ahead with its Final Frontier Tour following the departure of the band’s longtime drummer, Deen Castronovo.

“After careful consideration and an extensive year of touring, our talented, longtime drummer Deen Castronovo has decided to step away to focus on personal health matters that require his attention,” the “Open Arms” band revealed via a Friday, November 13, statement. “He has our full support during this time and extends his heartfelt thanks to the fans for the love, encouragement, and kindness he has received.”

The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductees have enlisted fill-in drummer Steve Murphy for the remainder of this year’s dates on Journey’s farewell tour.

“Native New Yorker Steve Murphy who comes to us from working with bands such as Alan Parsons Project, Trans Siberian Orchestra, Christopher Cross and Jack Bruce will be joining us for the remainder of November,” the band confirmed via Instagram. “We look forward to continuing to share unforgettable nights of music with all of you.”

Jon Bon Jovi Abruptly Ends NYC Concert Early: 'I'm Gonna Have to Cool It'

Castronovo’s shocking departure from Journey follows two recent incidents where he had to exit the stage mid-performance, forcing his bandmates to rearrange their show on the fly, with drum tech Steve Toomey ultimately filling in on both occasions.

Viral footage captured Journey announcing from the stage at the BOK Center in Tulsa on October 8 that Castronovo was being rushed to the hospital due to a “medical emergency” after performing only 2 songs in a planned 28-song setlist.

“We’re going to see what happens as this progresses,” Journey keyboardist and rhythm guitarist Jonathan Cain explained to fans that night. “It’s an unfortunate situation. We’re very sorry. We’re hoping it’s only a delay, but please — I’m sorry. Don’t worry. Have your prayers ready. Have your prayers ready for Deen Castronovo, everybody. Thank you.”

Journey frontman Arnel Pineda assured fans after an extended break that the drummer was “going to be fine.” Later in the show, lead guitarist Neal Schon dedicated the rest of the Tulsa show to Castronovo.

“This concert’s for Deen tonight,” he told the audience. “I’d love you all to pray for him. Everybody’s been going through a lot. I think he’s going to be fine.”

Castronovo was back on stage with Journey on October 10 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, though he was again rushed from the stage in Boston after performing 12 songs on Tuesday, November 10.

REO Speedwagon Retires From Touring Due to ‘Irreconcilable Differences’

Journey has not disclosed exactly what medical issues Castronovo is dealing with.

Prior to joining Journey in 1998, Castronovo played with singer John Waite and future Journey bandmates Schon, 72, and Cain, 76, in rock supergroup Bad English from 1987 to 1991. He later joined Ozzy Osbourne‘s backing band in 1995.

Journey’s Final Frontier Tour is set to wrap up for the year at the Honda Center in Anaheim on November 24.

title: ‘Poorly run, corrupt disasters’: President Donald Trump directs Vice President J.D. Vance to ‘focus his complete and total attention’ on ‘massive corruption and crime’ in Democrat-led cities and states
content:
President Donald Trump has directed Vice President J.D. Vance to focus on what he described as widespread corruption and crime in Democrat-led cities and states, singling out Minnesota, California and Illinois. In a Truth Social post on Thursday, November 12, Trump alleged that billions of dollars are being stolen every month and claimed that addressing the problem could quickly balance the federal budget. 

Donald Trump orders J.D. Vance to target alleged corruption in blue states

Trump announced the directive in a lengthy Truth Social post, accusing Democratic-led jurisdictions of widespread financial misconduct and poor administration. “I have asked Vice President Vance to focus his complete and total attention on the Massive Corruption and Crime taking place in Democrat run Cities and States throughout the U.S. The Blue States, such as Minnesota, California, Illinois, and many more, are all poorly run, corrupt disasters. Billions of Dollars is being stolen each and every month,” he wrote.

The president did not identify specific cases or provide evidence for his allegation that billions of dollars are being stolen monthly.

J.D. Vance already leads federal anti-fraud task force

Vance is already overseeing the White House’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, established by a March 16 executive order. The initiative coordinates federal efforts to strengthen eligibility checks, prevent improper payments and identify suspected fraud in government benefit programs. The order specifically identified Minnesota, California and Illinois as states where the administration alleged widespread fraud or vulnerabilities in benefit programs.

In October, reports said the task force was preparing to announce criminal charges against more than 40 defendants in an alleged $40 million Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) fraud scheme. It also reported identifying $260.7 billion in suspected fraud since Trump took office and preventing an estimated $72 billion in potentially fraudulent payments annually. However, those figures have not been independently verified.

Donald Trump claims tackling fraud could balance federal budget

Trump further argued that eliminating the alleged corruption could help resolve the country’s budget problems, writing, “Our Budget could be quickly BALANCED with the correction of this large scale criminal activity. CORRUPTION is in the Democrat Leadership’s blood!” However, he offered no explanation of how the alleged thefts were calculated or how recovering the money would balance the federal budget. It also remains unclear whether his latest instruction expands Vance’s existing responsibilities or simply places renewed emphasis on investigations involving Democratic-led jurisdictions.

Donald Trump pivots from domestic corruption to Iran

Trump concluded his post by shifting to the conflict with Iran, dismissing the prospect of further negotiations with the embattled nation. “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” Trump wrote. He did not elaborate on the claims about Iranian funds or the Strait of Hormuz, a strategically important waterway for global energy shipments.

title: 'Chicago Fire' Actress Robyn Coffin Announces Breast Cancer Diagnosis
content:
Chicago Fire actress Robyn Coffin is expected to undergo surgery after being diagnosed with breast cancer.

“Robyn has been diagnosed with breast cancer. Terrible news,” a statement on her GoFundMe page read. “The good news – she has a crack team at the hospital organizing and planning her surgery and aftercare and recovery.”

Coffin set up the fundraising page with friend Gianine DeFrancesco in hopes of supporting the actress through her upcoming operation and recovery. An initial fundraising goal has been set at $75,000, with more than $15,000 already raised as of publication.

“When Robyn doesn’t work, she doesn’t get paid,” DeFrancesco clarfied via GoFundMe. “So, this go fund me is not only to fill in the gaps that insurance will surely leave, but also to help sustain Robyn and [her husband] Grant while Robyn is off work. Thank goodness they have insurance, but let’s not get cocky – let’s give them a nest egg because we know there will be surprises.”

Baywatch’s Nicole Eggert Says More Cancer Was Found in Lymph Nodes

Coffin is expected to have a right partial mastectomy with magseed localization on December 3, followed by a course of radiation. First, she will meet with her care team on November 24 to make a final decision on whether a partial or full mastectomy will be the best treatment option.

“If that visit results in affirming the right partial mastectomy, Robyn is expecting to be out of work for 3 weeks,” DeFrancesco explained. “If a full mastectomy is required, Robyn’s time off work will increase quite a bit, as the surgery is much more extensive.”

Fans were assured in the fundraising appeal that Coffin will be able to count on her “husband Grant and supportive friends [as] wonderful caregivers.”

“We know that with insurance the surgery and hospital bill will amount to $40k. Because the surgery is hard upon, this amount is most urgent. The balance is for said surprises: a longer recovery period (see not working), medicine off the plan or not fully covered, or whatever is thrown at them,” DeFrancesco noted. “So, Village – thank you in advance for embracing Robyn with love and support. We’ve got her!”

Coffin’s Chicago Fire costar Miranda Rae Mayo shared a link via Instagram to the GoFundMe page to encourage donations, writing, “This beautiful and wonderful woman is in need of support. You may know her as Cindy Herrmann on our show. Any and everything helps.”

Mayo, 36, and fellow Chicago Fire cast member Hanako Greensmith — who play Stella Kidd and Violet Mikami, respectively — personally donated to help fund Coffin’s treatment.

Coffin is best known for playing Captain Christopher Herrmann‘s (David Eigenberg) wife Cindy Hermann on NBC’s long-running procedural hit Chicago Fire, having recurred or guest starred in each of the show’s 15 seasons. (The character also crossed over to Chicago Med for a 2016 episode.)

Having appeared in more than 60 episodes of Chicago Fire, Cindy’s most memorable story line involved her being diagnosed with lung cancer in season 11. Cindy underwent a grueling regimen of chemotherapy and radiation treatments before being declared cancer-free at the end of the season.

Coffin has also made supporting appearances on many hit shows throughout her career, including Empire and Under Covers.

title: Democratic California Gov. Gavin Newsom says he’ll announce in two months whether or not he’s running for president: ‘We’ll spend the next few weeks with the family and make a decision early January’
content:
California Gov. Gavin Newsom says he will decide by early January whether he intends to enter the 2028 presidential race, even as prediction markets show his standing among potential presidential contenders slipping. Speaking in Turkey on Thursday, November 12, Newsom said he would consult his family over the coming weeks before making his decision as he prepares to leave office in January.

Gavin Newsom sets early January deadline for presidential run decision

Speaking to Turkey’s Anadolu news agency while attending the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Newsom said he expects to settle the question within two months. “As it relates to 2028, we’ll make that decision in the next few months,” he said. “I’ll make the determination at the beginning of the year. So we’ll spend the next few weeks with the family and make a decision early January.”

Newsom, who is term-limited and leaves the California governorship in January, had previously avoided giving a specific timetable for his decision. He has also said that the support of his four children would be an important factor in deciding whether to run.

Kamala Harris could influence Gavin Newsom’s plans

A potential candidacy by former Vice President Kamala Harris, the 2024 Democratic presidential nominee, could complicate Newsom’s decision. In a September interview with CNN’s Jake Tapper, Newsom said he would not enter the race if Harris decides to run. “I don’t know if she runs, but we’ll see,” he said at the time.

Asked to clarify whether that meant he would stay in the contest, Newsom replied, “Of course not. Why would I? I wouldn’t do that to her. … I wouldn’t do that to you. I wouldn’t waste everyone’s time. Who needs that?” He also acknowledged that a contest between prominent Democrats could involve “mutual-assured destruction.”

Gavin Newsom celebrates Democratic midterm victories

Newsom’s announcement came shortly after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress, defeating Republicans in several traditionally GOP strongholds. He said he was “particularly pleased with the outcome of the election.”

“Donald Trump’s presidency, as we know it, ended last week in the U.S.,” he declared, describing the results as “a historic rebuke of his tenure.” He added that Democrats now had to govern and present voters with “a positive alternative agenda to Donald Trump.”

Prediction markets show Gavin Newsom losing ground

Despite his national profile and frequent clashes with Trump, Newsom’s prospects on prediction markets have weakened since the midterms. His chances of winning the Democratic nomination briefly fell to 7%, while the latest snapshot placed him at 11%, with more than $28.3 million in trading volume. Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff led at 27%, followed by Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez at 17%. Harris stood at 6%, while former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg and Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro each had 5%.

title: Virgin River's Shocking Exits Over the Years: Biggest Cast Changes
content:
Virgin River has gone through a surprising amount of cast exits through the years.

Based on Robyn Carr’s book series, Virgin River follows the lives of residents living in a small town in Northern California, including Mel (Alexandra Breckenridge) and Jack (Martin Henderson). The hit series, which premiered in 2019, also stars Colin Lawrence, Annette O’Toole, Tim Matheson, Benjamin Hollingsworth, Sarah Dugdale, Zibby Allen and Kai Bradbury.

After seven seasons, there have been some major departures from the Netflix show. Grayson Gurnsey left as Ricky after season 4, and Mark Ghanimé, who played Cameron, had a surprising exit once season 6 was released.

“I think this season saw a little bit of a sendoff for Cameron,” showrunner Patrick Sean Smith exclusively told Us Weekly in December 2024. “In terms of Mark, the actor who I adore, he unfortunately won’t be coming back for season 7.”

Which 'Virgin River' Stars Are — And Aren't — Returning After Cast Exits?

Smith didn’t rule out a potential return for the character in the future. “But that’s not to say that Cameron’s not a part of our world forever,” he added. “I would love to bring him back, and bring his character back when the story presents itself.”

In March 2026, Virgin River returned for season 7, and it was later confirmed that Marco Grazzini will not reprise his role as Mike. In another twist, Lauren Hammersley, who has played Charmaine since the show premiered, is also not expected to come back for season 8.

“For me, I’m just trying to look [at] the longevity of the show and making sure that the characters that we’re keeping have enough story engine in them to keep going,” Smith told Deadline at the time. “So I can’t say there are any specific cast shakeups planned, but I think we will have to start to — as characters run their course — make some decisions and bring in some new blood.”

The show was renewed for season 9 before season 8 premiered on Netflix.

content:
Russell Brand‘s ex Jordan Martin has alleged that the disgraced comedian once told her he “always wanted” to marry someone famous before dating his future wife Katy Perry.

“[Russell was] doing exactly what he always wanted to do [with Perry] and be married to someone famous, which he always said he would be,” Martin claimed in the new Netflix documentary Russell Brand: Open Secret.

Martin reportedly dated Brand, 51, for several months in 2007 while he was filming his breakthrough movie, Forgetting Sarah Marshall. In the documentary, Martin recalled that Brand summoned her to the movie’s set in Hawaii because he “wanted someone there to stop him from ‘trying it on’ with people on set,” per Page Six.

“He said to me I should be dating somebody more famous than you,” Martin recalled.

Katy Perry Seemingly Makes Joke About Justin Trudeau Romance

She accused Brand of turning their Hawaiian vacation into a traumatic experience by complaining that she was “dressing like an attention-seeking tart” and insisting he “didn’t feel comfortable” with her sunbathing.

Us has reached out to Brand and Perry’s representatives for comment.

Brand tied the knot with Perry, 42, in India in October 2010. Their marriage proved to be short-lived as he allegedly texted Perry a mere 14 months later in late 2011 to announce he was filing for divorce.

The “Watch It Burn” singer’s raw reaction to Brand’s devastating text message was caught on camera as she was filming her 2012 documentary Katy Perry: Part of Me at the time.

“In the very beginning of me getting into the industry, I would be out and about and I would hear girls, or actresses or musicians or whatever, they would say, ‘Oh no, I don’t want to be in a relationship because I don’t want to have to choose between being in a relationship and having a career,’” Perry explained in Part of Me. “I thought to myself, ‘Pfft, when I find that person that’s going to be my life partner, I will never have to choose because they’ll be accepting of me completely. … They won’t be threatened or have weird motives.’”

She continued, “[My partner] will be accepting of me, the things I love, the ambition, what I aspire to, what I want to create. They’ll be accepting and supportive. I started to realize, ‘Oh my God, that’s not true. That fairytale I had for me is not true for me right now.’”

In another unguarded moment, Perry insisted that she’d done “everything it takes to not fail” in her marriage to Brand.

“[The marriage] still failed,” she lamented. “The bad that comes along with the good is a journey and I learned so much from that journey.”

In a 2013 Vogue interview, Perry alleged that Brand struggled to see her as an “equal” when they were together.

“I felt a lot of responsibility for [the marriage] ending, but then I found out the real truth, which I can’t necessarily disclose because I keep it locked in my safe for a rainy day,” she teased at the time. “I let go and I was like: This isn’t because of me; this is beyond me.’ So I have moved on from that.”

Brand has also spoken publicly about his marriage breakdown over the years, including claiming on his “Stay Free With Russell Brand” podcast in 2025 that Perry was “not entirely normal.”

“She’s an extraordinary, massive star­ — but she’s not weird or off key,” he said at the time. “And wasn’t involved in anything nefarious, as far as I could tell. … The reasons that a marriage didn’t work are the normal human reasons [why] marriages don’t work, and I have nothing but respect for her.”

However, the Get Him to the Greek actor reacted harshly to Perry’s newfound romance with former Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, calling the politician a “globalist stooge.”

“I was OK with Orlando Bloom, but Justin Trudeau? Come on, man! Don’t put me in a category with that guy,” he sniped at a December 2025 Turning Point USA event.

Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison on Monday, November 9, after being convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He is being held in HMP Wandsworth in South London. (The comedian was accused of multiple instances of sexual abuse between 2004 and 2009 by four women.)

Prosecutors Couldn’t Mention Katy Perry in Russell Brand Rape Trial

In the wake of the verdict, London’s Metropolitan Police confirmed to Us that its officers were investigating additional rape allegations made by two unidentified women.

“The suspect has previously been interviewed under caution in connection with the allegations,” a Met spokesperson stated. “Files have been submitted to the Crown Prosecution Service in relation to both complainants.”

Brand has always maintained his innocence and has denied ever having nonconsensual sex.

title: Presley Gerber's Hollywood Home Reportedly Listed for $3.6M After His Death
content:
The late model Presley Gerber‘s 3,000 square-foot Hollywood Hills home is reportedly for sale following his shocking September death at age 27.

Real estate records reportedly indicate that the mid-century dwelling has been listed for $3.595 million, featuring four bedrooms and three baths in addition to outdoor and indoor living spaces, per TMZ.

With an impressive canyon view of the Hollywood Hills, the residence’s reported amenities include a jacuzzi, a cold plunge, a heated pool and a sauna. The property also features a separate guest house.

Gerber reportedly purchased the Los Angeles area home in March 2023 for $3.4 million.

Presley Gerber’s Sober Living Facility Investigated After His Death at Age 27

News broke on September 21 that Presley — son of supermodel Cindy Crawford and Casamigos co-founder Rande Gerber — died one day earlier from a suspected overdose while staying in a Santa Monica rehab center. (The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner confirmed to Us on September 21 that Presley’s cause of death was listed as “deferred” initially because its staff was in the “early stages of investigating” and that “limited information is currently available.”)

The Crawford-Gerber family asked for “privacy during this very difficult and painful time” in a statement obtained by Us on September 21.

Us subsequently learned that officers from the Santa Monica Police Department responded to a call regarding a possible overdose at an address matching the rehab facility on the day of Presley’s death.

“The Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner has identified the individual as Presley Gerber, 27,” a September 21 statement read. “SMPD detectives are investigating the death as a suspected overdose. At this time, there is no indication of foul play. The official cause and manner of death will be determined by the Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner.”

Presley had been open about his struggles with addiction and mental health, including speaking to reporters on a red carpet about his journey of self-acceptance just two months before his untimely death.

“The most free I felt was when I was finally honest with myself,” Presley said at a June We Are ENOUGH x Aviator Nation launch event. “Move your body regardless of how you’re feeling. Get outside. Get some sun. If you don’t feel like moving, lay on the grass.”

During a 2023 “Studio 22” podcast appearance, the Dolce & Gabbana and Ralph Lauren model stated his desire to help people struggling with addiction by sharing his story.

“Whether I help one person or a 100 people get out of that place that I was in at one point in my life, that’s all I need to do,” Presley told podcast listeners at the time. “I’ve had a lot of time to look into myself and learn about myself with therapists. I’ve seen a lot of stuff, and I’ve learned a lot of things, and what I hope I can do is have made the mistakes for some other people so they don’t have to make the same mistakes that I made.”

His parents, Crawford and Randy, 60 and 64 respectively, broke their silence about Presley’s death in October by sharing a new statement reflecting on their son’s life.

“Presley Walker Gerber. July 2, 1999-September 20, 2026. We are beyond heartbroken to lose our beloved son and brother. We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years. He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever,” the couple wrote in a joint statement shared on October 18. “We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability. We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain. Til we meet again our sweet boy.”

Inside Kaia Gerber's Relationship With Late Brother Presley Gerber

The same month, Presley’s sister, model and actress Kaia Gerber, penned her own poignant memorial post about the ongoing process of grieving.

“Prez, I don’t have the words, and maybe the tiny mercy is that we didn’t need them all along. Words fail and words subtract and words summarize and words always lack truth. And how naive of me to believe that language could transcend grief,” Kaia, 25, wrote via an October 18 Instagram post. “I’ve read all of the books and I have none of the answers. My articulation is no match against this, the magnitude of losing you. I am, quite literally, down on my f***ing knees.”

The Shards star described her late brother as “inherently good,” adding that she considered herself to be Presley’s “lucky eternal witness” throughout their lives.

“My best buddy, my great protector, the hardest I’ve ever laughed and the one true love of my life — you lit all of my candles and took all of my monsters away. And I love you. And I love you. And I love you. Only you know how much. Thank you for being here,” she concluded.

Mortensen dated show star Taylor Frankie Paul on and off during the first five seasons of the Hulu series. The exes, who welcomed son Ever in March 2024, split for good in fall 2025 when Paul, 32, went to film The Bachelorette season 22.

Paul’s season was ultimately pulled days before its March premiere after footage footage of her 2023 arrest for domestic violence resurfaced, showing the influencer hitting and throwing chairs at her ex in the presence of her children. (Paul pleaded guilty to aggravated assault in exchange for the dismissal of additional charges pertaining to child abuse. She completed her three-year probation earlier this year.)

'Mormon Wives' Halts Filming Amid Taylor and Dakota Dispute: What to Know

A judge has since granted Mortensen sole custody of Ever, with Paul receiving visitation rights. Mortensen, who has not publicly addressed the lawsuit, argued in his court petition that Mormon Wives portrayed him as “a domestic abuser” and a “serial adulterer” who retaliated against Taylor by calling Child Protective Services (CPS). Russell Brand Admits to Having Sex With 16-Year-Old When He Was 30

I was devastated by it.”

Back in April, Brand admitted to having sex with a 16-year-old when he was 30 during an interview with former Fox News host Megyn Kelly.

“The plain fact of it is that in Europe and in the United Kingdom, where I’m from, the age of consent is 16. And I did sleep with a 16-year-old when I was 30,” Brand said while appearing on The Megyn Kelly Show at the time. “When I was 30, I was a very different person. I was a lot younger, and I was an immature 30-year-old.” (The age of consent in the U.K. was 16 in 2006 and remains so to this day. Brand has repeatedly denied any sexual wrongdoing.)

“He was a very successful man who had a lot of power and sway in the industry,” Latter told the outlet, responding to Brand’s comments on Kelly’s podcast. “Whereas I was a 16-year-old with no life experience, no sexual experience and no prior relationships. What was my level of maturity meant to be?”

Months later, the comedian was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for rape and sexual assault. Kelly, 55, quickly came to the disgraced comedian’s defense in the wake of his conviction and subsequent prison sentence.

“I don’t believe the charges,” Kelly said during the Monday, November 9, episode of her YouTube show. “And I don’t have to believe them just because the jury came through with the opposite conclusion. I feel indignant that this obvious conservative stalwart has been targeted.”

The former journalist added, “And he had backdoor sex with a woman who licked his backdoor before she was even introduced to him. This is insane.”

Latter told The Times she decided to go public with her identity in an effort to change consent laws.

“I just don’t know what capacity I have to give years more of my life to this, for my head to be occupied with these awful crimes,” she said. “And it takes a toll on your personal life, on your marriage. She continued, “It’s shocking to me time and time again that whenever the news comes up again about him, it’s always in the comments about the relationship with a 16-year-old. That’s not the most heinous bit. But why is that the thing that everybody collectively gets stuck on? title: Tiffani Thiessen, 52, Says She Needs Hip Replacement After Sharing Diagnosis
content:
Tiffani Thiessen is opening up about her health issues after dealing with a slew of admittedly painful conditions.

“I have to get a hip replacement — I do,” the Saved by the Bell alum, 52, said on the Tuesday, November 10, episode of Tom Papa’s eponymous podcast. “I was a dancer when I was younger, which was a good thing, [and] I have a torn labrum, that’s one issue I have. Then, I found out, going to my second opinion, … I have hip dysplasia.”

Hip dysplasia, according to the Cleveland Clinic, occurs when bones in the hip joint no longer properly fit together.

“So, when I was very flexible as a young child has now caused my issue now,” she quipped. “I  hear the hip replacements aren’t as bad as knee and shoulders [replacement procedures].”

Tiffani Thiessen Shares Her Biggest Parenting Challenge While Raising 2 Kids

According to Theissen, she has been in so much pain that she’s unable to carry out certain tasks, including a friendly game of pickleball.

“We play [as a family],” the actress, who shares two kids with husband Brady Smith, added. “My doctor didn’t say it was pickleball, but it probably is not help[ful]. I have not been able to play in the last couple weeks ‘cause my hip’s been so bad.”

Theissen has also recently been splitting her time between California and Vancouver, Canada, while filming her new show, Disney+’s Coven Academy.

“It’s a great city. I am in the same time zone so that’s helpful for my family, and it’s an easy flight so I try to come home. I never go more than two weeks without seeing my family,” she said of working in the Canadian city. “It’s definitely an adjustment. It’s not what I love, two weeks is big [but] Mama’s got to work.”

Tiffani Thiessen's Teenager Thinks 'Beverly, Hills 90210' Is Too 'Slow'

Coven Academy, in which Thiessen plays headmistress Emma Graves, was recently greenlit for a second season.

“Season 1 was a huge cliffhanger with my character, so, you find out a big sort of connection between me and the lead girl, and so that’s going to be, probably, something they’re going to have to deal with in season 2,” the actress teased of Emma being revealed as the birth mother of Malina Pauli Weissman’s Briar Roberts. “The baggage of season 1 goes to season 2. Lots of cliffhangers for a lot of the characters actually, but mine was the big one at the end.”

Thiessen’s role on Coven Academy has even impressed her real-life kids: Harper, 16, and Holt, 11.

“I’m always trying to make sure I’m cool in their eyes, which is not always the case,” she said. “I think my daughter when I got this job, there’s a kid on the show, his name is Malachi Barton, and he’s this huge [young star and] the girls love him, very handsome, very cool guy, dancer, you know, all this.”

When Thiessen filmed the pilot episode with Barton, 19, she said her daughter freaked out.

“My daughter [was] like, ‘Hey, who’s on the show with you, Mom?’ And so, I went down the cast and I got to Malachi and she goes, ‘Wait, I’m sorry, what?’ I go, ‘Yeah, this kid named Malachi Barton is super cute.’ She’s like, ‘Mom, I follow him. He is a massive influencer.’”

title: Broad City's Abbi Jacobson Says She and Wife Pose as 'Sisters' to Stay Safe
content:
Broad City star Abbi Jacobson is opening up about the way she safely travels with her wife, Jodi Balfour, through notoriously anti-LGBTQ states as a gay couple.

“As my wife and I drive, if we drive across the country, there are states where we are sisters. In case,” Jacobson, 42, told Page Six during a Tangles screening earlier this week.

“It’s really wild, how we’ve come so far in a lot of areas,” she added, while acknowledging that “many people” are not able to hide their sexuality in order to protect their physical safety and wellbeing.

Jacobson met Balfour, 39, virtually in 2020 during the deadly COVID-19 pandemic. At the time, Balfour was navigating the loss of a sibling and a previous breakup. The pair went public with their romance in October 2021 and after keeping their relationship secret for a year. They later tied the knot at the Public Records in Brooklyn in 2024.

Sarah and Holland! Hollywood's Gay Power Couples

“After so much distance, we wanted the wedding to feel like that first sweaty shoulder moment — total togetherness,” Balfour told Cultured of the pair’s intimate wedding at the time. “I think we did that.”

“It was such kismet because the ceremony was not what we expected, but it was exactly what we’d hoped for,” Jacobson added of their ceremony. “People were packed together. When we looked out at the audience, our friends were on stools, peeking through the plants, and sitting on top of the booths. I’ve never been to a wedding like that.”

While legal and cultural strides have been made regarding the LGBTQ+ community in recent years — including the 2015 U.S. Supreme Court ruling establishing the Constitutionally-protected right for same-sex couples to get married — hate crimes against LGBTQ+ people are on the rise.

According to data published by the Federal Bureau of Investigations (FB), hate crimes targeting LGBTQ+ individuals have increased for the past four years in a row. In 2022, after the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade, Justice Clarence Thomas wrote a concurring opinion in which he explicitly suggested the Court “reconsider” Obergefell v. Hodges, the landmark case granting LGBTQ+ people the right to marry nationwide.

'Red, White & Royal Blue' Joins the Best Onscreen LGBT+ Love Stories

According to the ACLU’s bill tracker, over 500 anti-LGBTQ+ state bills have been considered across various U.S. state legislatures in 2026 alone — the majority targeting trans people and their legal right to access gender-affirming care or participate on sport teams that align with their gender identity.

“I do think that representation is a little bit on my mind,” Jacobson told The Independent in a 2022 interview discussing her decision to go public with her relationship. “Not to say that I’m posting a photo of us to be like, ‘We need people to know that there are queer people out there.’ I’m not doing that. But I am sort of! I don’t feel like there’s a ton of us in the industry.”

She continued at the time, “You just hope you can open up people’s minds and also get people who don’t feel seen to feel seen and empowered.”

title: Valerie Bertinelli, 66, Flaunts Bare Midsection Amid Weight Loss Journey
content:
Valerie Bertinelli is proudly showing off her ongoing weight loss journey.

“#ootd feelin good 😊,” Bertinelli, 66, captioned a Tuesday, November 10, Instagram video, revealing the ensemble she wore for her recent Drew Barrymore Show appearance.

Bertinelli paired dark Mersea wide-leg jeans with a gray, cap-sleeve BCBG sweater from Macy’s and tortoiseshell glasses.

As the Food Network star offered a glimpse of her ‘fit, she casually lifted up the hem of her sweater to reveal her bare midsection.

Valerie Bertinelli Rewears ‘Fat Clothes’ From Jenny Craig Photo: 'F—ked Up'

Bertinelli received a flurry of support in the comments section.

“Feeling good and looking even better! That sweater is a whole vibe! 💕✨,” the official Macy’s account replied, while the BCBG brand added, “Look good feel good – will channel this energy all week long 💌.”

Another fan chimed in, “Freaking gorgeous. You also look beautiful.”

Bertinelli has long been candid about her body image and weight loss experiences, revealing in 2023 that she went “down a size” after cutting out alcohol from her diet.

View this post on Instagram

“So, here’s a nice little side effect of Dry January. These jeans that I’m wearing were so tight a few months ago that I couldn’t comfortably button them,” she said in a February 2023 TikTok video. “Now, they’re so loose it’s time for me to go down a size. Yeah, I like that side effect.”

Even amid Bertinelli’s slimdown, she has taken issue with any body-shaming comments.

“Someone … decided to point out that I needed to lose weight because, see, I don’t have a scale or I don’t have clothes that I’m trying to put on every day,” the One Day at a Time alum sarcastically joked in a 2021 social media video. “I needed that help to let me know that I need to lose weight.”

According to Bertinelli, such feedback is “not helpful” in the slightest.

Valerie Bertinelli Recalls How She Was ‘Considered Overweight’ at 150 Lbs

“When you see somebody who has put some weight on, my first thought is, ‘That person is obviously going through some things,’” she said at the time. “But since I haven’t been successful with that my whole entire life — at 61 I’m still dealing with [it]. You think I’m not tired of it, lady? Where is the compassion? Not f***ing helpful.”

Bertinelli previously tied her weight gain to grieving the deaths of her parents and ex Eddie Van Halen.

“I’ve used food as a way not to feel the sadness or the stress. But by eating something away, all it does is make me feel worse about myself,” she wrote in a 2020 essay for Today. “One of my personal mottos is ‘choose happy.’ But sometimes that choice is really challenging. To me, I think that joy is tied to making healthy choices with my life in everything I do. Healthy in the people I surround myself with, the food I eat and, perhaps most importantly, the way I talk to myself.”

title: YouTuber Grace Helbig Gives Update on Stage 4 Cancer After Brain Surgery
content:
YouTube star Grace Helbig opened up about her ongoing stage IV breast cancer battle.

“It has been a month since my brain surgery to remove two tumors from my brain,” Helbig, 41, said in a Friday, November 13, video shared via TikTok. “Healing has been going great.”

Helbig was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2023, subsequently undergoing a lumpectomy. While Helbig went into remission after her treatment, she revealed in October that the tumors had metastasized and spread to her brain. She underwent brain surgery later that month.

“If this was 20 years ago, I think this would be very scary but science and medicine has advanced in so many ways,” Helbig acknowledged of her prognosis. “Now, stage IV is often treated like a chronic illness. Wild, but let me be clear, I am stage IV metastatic breast cancer, however, I am NED, which stands for no evidence of disease.”

Jessie J and More Stars Who Beat Breast Cancer

Despite being declared cancer-free, Helbig has faced “lingering anxiety” over the possibility that her cancer will return.

“Every time I get a mammogram, every time I’ve gone for an MRI, [I worried] that there would be [a] recurrence,” she admitted. “The positive side, I’ve been through this before and I’ve had this ghost of breast cancer past, sort of, following me around to my medical appointments. I wasn’t totally thrown off guard by the fact that it had recurred.”

Helbig has since found community with fellow breast cancer survivors, praising how the patients continue to have “fulfilling lives” amid their own stage IV diagnoses.

Celebrity Health Scares Through the Years

“I now get to enter their elite group of metastatic badasses,” she stated. “Seeing them the last few years has really primed me to understand that it is paradoxically possible to live beautiful, relatively normal …  lives with stage IV metastatic breast cancer. Things have lined up in very interesting ways the last few years, which has made all of this, right now, a lot more palatable than I think it could have been. I’m very grateful for that.”

Helbig completed her fifth round of radiation treatment earlier this month and said she still feels “very optimistic” about her next steps.

“Now is the part of my treatment plan where I am trying to figure out what will be my treatment moving forward,” she noted. “I think this [journey] has been teaching me how to say yes to very uncertain moments that you couldn’t really plan for. It’s definitely made me much more malleable, much more flexible and, through that process, I think more resilient.”
